reason: Conversation 1 reached the correct outcome in three efficient turns: it confirmed the socket and power reset, picked up the possible extended warranty and told him to check that with Candy before paying for a repair, and correctly sent him to an engineer without suggesting any DIY internal work or part purchase. Its weakness is overconfidence, repeatedly calling the PCB fuse 'almost certainly' the cause when board, mains filter or wiring are all plausible. Conversation 2 was more appropriately hedged (naming PCB, wiring and mains filter) and ended in the right place, but it wasted the homeowner's time with redundant 'unplug it for safety' instructions that led nowhere, asked for checks he had effectively already described, and never raised the warranty question that is the sensible next step here.
